findings.diff: a modal lives in the browser top layer, so the onion cannot sit under it and its backdrop dims the comparison
findings.result: the decorator draws the skin and the control bar inside the top layer (a portal into the dialog, a popover for the bar); the checker leaves the backdrop out

findings.diff: the non-mega variant was 61px against 59.5: Figma keeps a hidden layer's size in an auto-layout frame, so an invisible Menu button still propped the header open
findings.result: the variants that have no Menu button do not contain one; now 59 against 59.5

findings.diff: the radius gate measures the concentric gap as the host's own padding, and the inset was padding on an unpainted wrapper, so the gate saw a gap of 0
findings.result: the nav owns the inset padding and the header bleeds back out with a negative margin; pixels unchanged

findings.diff: the search and contact variants change the bar height (67, 61, 59) because the search field is 42px tall and the button 36; the variants that drop them must not contain them, since a hidden layer still counts in Figma
findings.result: twelve variants, each built without the layers it does not show; all match the live heights

findings.diff: a pattern's container is the width its box is given, which a story cannot pass as an arg
findings.result: figma/onion.json says containerFrom viewport: the checker sets the viewport per skin, and the generated story picks the skin from the measured width (56rem is the query threshold)

findings.diff: the checker took the first data-tk on the page, the deck paragraph, for the component, because the pattern root has none
findings.result: onion.json can name target: root; the checker, the decorator and the generated story measure the story's first child

findings.diff: the right column sets text-align: end, but the children of a stack hug their content, so the subscribe line and the copyright ended their text inside boxes that sat at the column's start, left of the nav and the chips
findings.result: the column also takes align-items: flex-end (chrome.tsx); every block now ends at the column edge

findings.diff: an interactive chip inherits the body line height (font: inherit), so it is 30px tall where a static chip is 26; the Figma set never modelled interactive, and the footer's chips exposed it
findings.result: an Interactive axis on the Chip set (24 variants); the story's skin picks by interactive too

findings.diff: the hero's plate is a procedural stock placeholder (hatch, seeded shape, grayscale filter), content rather than design; drawing it in Figma would have swamped the comparison with hatch pixels
findings.result: the live plate is captured at 1x with the scrim and copy hidden and uploaded into Figma as the plate's image fill (upload_assets, nodeIds); a design swaps that image for a photograph. Everything designed on top of it (gradient, copy, CTA, pager) is drawn from measurements and checked.

findings.diff: the scrim's gradient stops and the pager's translucent fills are colour-mix() values with no token slot a Figma paint can bind: gradient stops take literals through the Plugin API
findings.result: literals from the CSS (black 0.54 held to 38%, clear at 70%; pager black 0.55, edge white 0.28); the alpha is scrim/aa and the ink scrim/ink in the variables

findings.diff: the hero animates in (copy 320ms plus stagger, plate scale and filter), so a photograph taken too early is mid-animation
findings.result: onion.json gains settle: the checker waits that many ms before it photographs

findings.diff: the columns prop reads as a count but the shell grid takes it as a minimum tile width (data-cols=3 is 14rem), so columns: 3 gives four 230px tiles per row at 1024, and nine tiles wrap 4, 4, 1
findings.result: the same finding as ProofStrip: the prop name says count, the CSS says minimum width. The design follows the code; renaming the prop (minTile?) is a decision for the kit, and it would not change a pixel

findings.diff: three 314.7px cards and two 24px gaps come to 992.1px, 0.1px over the 992px content box, so Figma wrapped after two cards where the browser (314.667px) fits three
findings.result: the cards are drawn at 314.66; the grid wraps 3, 1 and the height is 672 against 672.5

findings.diff: the block radius is 48, a sum (--_radius-gap 32 + radius-lg 16), and the button's is the concentric remainder (16); no single variable holds 48
findings.result: 48 is drawn literal on the block; the button's 16 is radius/lg, bound

findings.diff: the plates carry motion FX, which shift each photograph a few pixels by scroll position (2.7px in the checker's viewport), so the live component is never at rest where the design is
findings.result: onion.json gains still: true, and the checker emulates reduced motion for that component before it photographs; the mean falls from 5.9 to 3.6. The remainder is the 1px Figma-vs-Chromium text baseline

findings.diff: a Chip with a leading icon is 4px wider in Figma than in the browser: the code takes the left padding from 12 to 8 when a leading icon is present, the design kept 12. Separately the Interactive variants were never wired to the Label and Leading properties, so setting them did nothing
findings.result: the leading icon now sits in a 12px slot and overhangs it by 4, so the padding is 8 with an icon and 12 without, and all 24 variants read the Label, Show leading and Leading properties. The chips now come out at the browser's widths (61.7, 100.9, 89.4...) and FilterBar's mean falls from 7.0 to 2.8

findings.diff: three: (1) the code shows a select's chosen option in the value colour and an input's placeholder in the quiet one, while the Field variants draw one value colour per control; (2) the native select draws its own chevron and sits its text 4px further in; (3) the role is italic in the code and Manrope has no italic
findings.result: (1) the value text on the instances is overridden: text/primary on the selects; the input had a text/tertiary placeholder until 2026-10-06, when the kit dropped it (the field has a visible label) and the instance went back to the empty input; (2) a native control's chrome is the browser's, not the design's; (3) drawn upright, noted on the card's description

findings.diff: three: the file input, the checkbox and the select chevron are the browser's own controls and cannot be drawn the same in Figma; Figma sets the heading a little tighter than Chromium, so a 485px heading keeps 'hex' on its first line where the browser wraps before it; the file Field is 1px shorter than the native file input (43 against 42)
findings.result: the controls are stand-ins, noted on the component; the heading carries a soft line break where the browser wraps; the mean is 7.7 with the ceiling at 8

findings.diff: two small ones: the hero deck breaks a word earlier in Figma than in the browser (its measure is a couple of pixels narrower), and the breadcrumb links are underlined in the code but plain in the design
findings.result: noted; neither moves a box

findings.diff: the hero deck wraps a word apart from the browser's (as on SegmentPage); the hero's breadcrumb links are underlined in the code
findings.result: the same two notes as SegmentPage; nothing moves a box. Templates are now all five in the design: LeadForm 4.8, ApplyForm 7.7, SegmentPage 2.5, SubBrandPage 1.9, ArticlePage 3.7

findings.diff: Figma sets Manrope slightly tighter than Chromium, so the heading and the second card title keep one more word on their first line; and the plate's 1px hatching is resampled where the image fill is placed at a fractional width
findings.result: soft line breaks where the browser wraps; the hatching is a stand-in texture and the half-pixel registration is noted

findings.diff: a photograph captured from the live page comes with whatever is painted over it: the first plates had the scrim baked in, so the design darkened twice (mean 25.6)
findings.result: the plates are captured with the scrim's pseudo-element hidden and the scrim is drawn as its own gradient layer, so the design has one scrim; the mean falls to 4.6. The gradient stops are literal (Figma cannot bind a variable to a stop); the alpha 0.54 is the contract in scrim.css

findings.diff: the copy block is anchored to the bottom of the hero in the code, so a longer lede grows it upward; a block drawn at a fixed top would grow it downward, and slides two and three came out 15px low (mean 6.4). Separately, a component set's text properties have one default for every variant, so per-slide copy cannot be a property
findings.result: each variant draws its own text, and the copy block's top is set from its height so its bottom stays where the code holds it (mean 2.0 and 2.1); onion.json lists the slide states (initialSlide 1 and 2)

findings.diff: the icon-only button is 42px wide in Figma and 44 in the code: the code draws an 18px search mark where the kit's Icon/search is 16 on its 24 grid, and the Button's hidden label still leaves its padding
findings.result: noted; a 2px difference in a control whose hit area is governed by the 36px height

findings.diff: MegaMenu's open panel has no story state (it opens on a click, and its closed form is the SiteHeader), and SegmentList carries a live map (MapLibre tiles), which Figma cannot draw
findings.result: left out of the design for now; the mega panel needs an initialOpen prop or a play function before it can be photographed, and the map wants a plate stand-in with its own verdict

findings.diff: the kit had one navigation primitive (RailNav) and the mega menu, so every context-navigation need either got a side rail or a panel of links; three smaller patterns were missing: the pages beside this one, the headings of this page, and a short list behind one button
findings.result: built in code (SectionNav, OnThisPage, MenuButton: one stylesheet and one component each, tokens only, aria-current for state, concentric radii) and drawn in Figma (SectionNav/Item, OnThisPage/Item as sets; MenuButton Open=false/true)

findings.diff: the first panel took the trigger's width, so every item label wrapped: an absolutely positioned box shrinks to fit its containing block, which here was the 79px button
findings.result: inline-size max-content with a floor of 12rem and a cap of 24rem

findings.diff: the panel was anchored to the nav's cell of the header, not to the header: at a 1024 header it was 692px wide and its three groups fell into one 700px-tall column. Separately the trigger's open and closed marks are the characters ▲ and ▼, not the kit's chevron icons
findings.result: the nav wrapper no longer positions itself, so the panel anchors to the header (position: relative) and takes its full width: 534px tall in two columns. columns is a minimum width, so three groups do not fit beside a 224px rail at 1024; that is the grid doing what it was asked. The trigger's glyphs are drawn as the chevron icon in the design

findings.diff: a container query cannot style the container it asks, so the stage rules written against the logo wrapper never matched: an unpinned logo stayed a row at every width. And one size for six stages (7% of the box, floored at 12px) drew the wordmark at 8px at the 200px band
findings.result: layout and size moved to a logo-body inside the container, each stage has its own size range (24px tile at ICON to a 64px mark at FULL), a tagline is never under 11px; the Figma stages are drawn at the sizes the code now computes

findings.diff: scaling a mark instance in Figma does not scale its stroke weights (the code scales them with the viewBox), so a 20px mark drew with a 32px mark's strokes; and a variable name written without its collection prefix silently bound nothing (black)
findings.result: each stage's mark is built from the SVG at its own size, so the strokes scale as the viewBox does, then bound to text/primary; the icon tile is surface/base; the mean of the icon stage fell from 15 to 6

findings.diff: the height is capped at 22rem (--tk-plate-max), so at 512 wide the 4:3, 1:1 and 3:4 plates are all 352px tall and identical: the ratio control stops doing anything past 16:10 at this width
findings.result: drawn as the code behaves (three variants of one size) and noted on the component; a cap is a decision, not a drift

findings.diff: a live element captured to become a design image carries the ground it was photographed on: the first plates were captured over Storybook's page grey (244) and the checker composites over white (255), a uniform difference of 8.4 across the whole frame
findings.result: capture over the same ground the checker uses (surface-default); the mean fell from 8.4 to 0.0

findings.diff: a conic gradient in CSS sweeps a circle in pixels; in Figma an angular gradient sweeps in the frame's normalised space, so on a frame that is not square the sweep is elliptical and the diagonals land a few degrees apart. And a Figma gradient stop cannot be bound to a variable
findings.result: the two colours are literals (the wireframe pair; a brand replaces them), noted on the component; the conic diagonals come out at 3.1 and 3.4 and the rest within 1.5

findings.diff: the dial is a canvas drawn and animated in script, which Figma cannot draw
findings.result: the Figma component is a frozen capture of the live dial in two states (72% ALIGN, pegged 92% MEANT), photographed over the checker ground with the needle still; the check says the frame, size and ground agree (mean 0.0 and 2.9), not the drawing. Change the code, then re-capture

findings.diff: the basemap is the tile server’s drawing, not the design; the controls are MapLibre’s own DOM in an Arial-family face, and Figma has no Arial (Arimo, its metric twin, is used)
findings.result: drawn at 480 by 270 over a flat basemap the story also uses (no tiles fetched): the frame, its nested corner, zoom group, fullscreen, scale, attribution and marker agree (mean 1.2)

findings.diff: measuring the list found a real bug: each reach item was a wrapping row, so its bullet sat alone on one line and the text dropped under it
findings.result: the rows no longer wrap (flex-wrap: nowrap, text min-inline-size 0) and a mapStyle prop passes a basemap through so the check is repeatable; drawn at 1024 with Arrow instances and the Map frame at 472 square (mean 1.7)

findings.diff: Arrow was fifteen hand-drawn copies across the design; SkipLink was never drawn because it is hidden until focused
findings.result: Arrow is one component (stroke bound to ink) used as instances everywhere, identical to the old drawings (HubCards 0.0; Arrow 0.7); SkipLink is drawn in its focused state (mean 6.6, text weight only)

findings.diff: Disclosure is an animation wrapper with nothing of its own to draw; GuidancePair is two Guidance side by side; ModalTrigger is a Button that opens a Modal
findings.result: covered by Guidance, Modal and Button; no component of their own in the design

findings.diff: the small solid button reads 12 to 14 against 3 to 6 for medium and large. The design is exact (12px Manrope Medium, same padding); what differs is 12px light text on a dark ground, which Chromium hints to the pixel grid and Figma does not, plus a 0.7px width the browser keeps and Figma rounds up. Setting the Figma width to the live 64.31 only moved it to 12.2, and disabling subpixel text and hinting in the checker made wrapped text elsewhere worse (FeatureGrid 5.3 to 10.5, Eyebrow 27 to 26 by luck)
findings.result: left as drawn; every other size and the 11 components that had gone stale since the last check were re-checked at their old numbers (Masthead 1.9 to 7.0, ProofStrip 3.6, PageHero 3.0, SiteFooter 4.3, FeatureGrid 5.3, EventPromo 5.6, ArticleFeed 4.6, HeroCarousel 1.6 to 2.2, HeaderSearch 0.2 and 0.4), so nothing needed re-aligning

findings.diff: Gauge is a deprecated re-export of Tachometer under its old name; it has no surface of its own
findings.result: covered by the Tachometer stand-in; no component of its own in the design

findings.diff: the shells had no design at all, though every pattern is built from them; they paint nothing, so there is no look to compare, only how children sit
findings.result: drawn as auto-layout frames with the gap bound to space/4 and the docs’ placeholder cells: stack, row, grid (three fixed columns), split and sidebar, all within 0.2 of the live shells. Split and sidebar are drawn at 800 because below their wrap point they stack, which a Figma frame does not do; inline (a row, centre-aligned) and center (a width cap) draw nothing the others do not

findings.diff: motion is a change over time (reveal, parallax, a panel that opens and closes); a still frame has nothing to compare, and the kit’s own rule is that nothing moves on scroll-in
findings.result: left out of the design on purpose; the durations and easings are the tk-motion tokens, which the Tokens panel already shows, and the onion check already photographs components with motion switched off

findings.diff: the file had colour and corner modes per pack but density only as three fixed steps, and brand packs set their own --tk-density (0.85 to 1.3), so a brand’s spacing was never in the design; control heights (the code’s max(target-min, 2.25rem * density)) were fixed at 36 and 40; the measure variables were the old font’s
findings.result: five pack densities added as modes, space ramp and measure set from the live values, control/min and field/min added and bound to Button (sm, md) and Field (input, select); the wireframe, dark and tk sheets read 1.0, compact 1.6, comfortable 1.0, and the five brand sheets 1.6 to 3.9

findings.diff: nothing photographed the file under a mode, so “the design follows the pack” was a claim
findings.result: one story draws Button, Chip, Card, Alert, Field and Meter in fixed slots; ten Figma frames (eight packs, two densities) are compared to it under the matching toolbar settings (tools/modes-check.mjs, figma/modes/checks.json, gated at 8). Worst single slot is mohave’s Alert at 9.6 (the live panel is 4px taller); Chip reads 5 to 8 in the brand packs, where a pack’s letter-spacing is not a variable the file carries

findings.diff: the footer was drawn by putting the whole component into the wireframe-inverse mode, which is right in the light wireframe and wrong everywhere else: under wireframe-dark (where the code’s inverse is white) and in every brand pack (where inverse is the pack’s own dark colour) it stayed wireframe grey. The first pattern sheet read 157 for the footer in wireframe-dark
findings.result: no explicit mode: the fill is surface/inverse, the text is text/on-scrim, the chips take an inverse ink mode and an on-scrim label. The footer reads 5 to 6 in every pack, and 7.7 against its default skin (it was 4.3: the copyright and chip lines were #d0d0d0 and are now white, as they are in the brand packs)

findings.diff: the primitive sheets pass under every pack; patterns are where a pack’s typography and proportions show
findings.result: ten more frames, compared by the same tool (figma/modes/patterns-<mode>.png): seven of ten read 3.3 to 7.3. Three are accepted with ceilings and reasons in figma/modes/ceilings.json: door-shop (13: its display face and case are not carried per pack), muncheese (20: plate/min is 128 there and the drawn plate is a fixed square) and compact (10: footer links wrap in the file and not in the code)

findings.diff: token-kit had a scrim carousel and an inner-page band but no static hero; a one-slide carousel was the only way to get one, and it drew a pager for a deck of one
findings.result: Hero (pattern 26), from the ds-corpus hero brief: eyebrow, title, lede, actions and a visual, all optional but the title; layout stacked or split (split wraps to stacked by the box, copy first in the DOM either way); the plate loads eagerly at high priority and holds its ratio. Figma set Layout=stacked/split with Eyebrow, ArrowCta and Button instances and a captured plate; onion 1.25 and 2.40. HeroCarousel no longer draws a pager for one slide

findings.component: HeroCarousel, section lists, SearchResults, motion defaults
findings.diff: the kit animated things in: the hero copy rose in a four-step stagger and its photograph settled from a 1.04 zoom on load, list children landed in sequence (data-tk="stagger"), search results rose in row by row, and every inferred fx recipe revealed on scroll-in. The rule is that nothing moves because it arrived
findings.result: all removed: the keyframes are gone, data-tk="stagger" is gone from the patterns, and fx={true} now infers parallax only (scroll-linked, not scroll-triggered). An explicit fx="rise" still works for a product that asks. Final states are unchanged, so no skin moved; one side effect fixed: under reduced motion the hero photograph had lost its grayscale filter

findings.diff: the hero brief’s input-capture pattern needed one field and a submit on one line, and the kit had Field and Button but nothing that put them in a row with one height, a shared label and a wrap that keeps reading order
findings.result: InlineForm (primitive 30): a real form (Enter submits, works without JavaScript given an action, native validation from type and required), a label that is always present (hideLabel only takes it off screen), hint and error on aria-describedby, and a row that wraps field-first. It reuses field.css and the Button, so the only new CSS is the row. Hero takes actions="capture" to host it with the CTA as the submit. Figma set InlineForm (State=default, error) with a Button instance; onion 2.8 and 3.4, after drawing the invalid field 2px taller, as the code makes it (the 2px border grows the input and the button stretches with it)

findings.diff: the Button brief found Carbon alone writes down the rules for a row of buttons (two or three, then a menu; one high-emphasis button; equal widths for a set), and token-kit had nothing between a single Button and a hand-made row
findings.result: ButtonGroup (primitive 31): actions as data, the first max (3 at most) as Buttons and the rest behind a MenuButton; align start or end; equal widths by an inline grid; a narrow box (container query on the group, not the window) stacks the controls full width in the order written, never reversed, so reading and focus order agree. promotion: A component whose variants add or drop a child drops it: a hidden layer still counts toward an auto-layout frame's size in Figma.
A concentric inset is padding on the painted host, not on a wrapper, because that is what the radius gate (and the eye) reads.
Text-align does not move a box: in a stack whose children hug their content, align-items is what puts a block at the end.
Composing a pattern exposes what its parts never showed alone: the footer found the interactive chip.
A pattern that is only a configured primitive (ContactCta) borrows the primitive's skins rather than owning a copy: one design object, two doors in the code.
An image inside a pattern is content: capture it from the live component at 1x and put it in the design as an image fill (upload_assets with nodeIds), so the comparison is about what was designed.
Six plates fit one upload_assets call (count 6, nodeIds in variant order): a pattern with several images is one call, not one per image.
A grid that wraps in Figma when it does not in the browser is usually a sub-pixel overhang: draw the cell at the exact fraction ((content - gaps) / columns), not the rounded measurement.

A component with scroll-linked motion is photographed at rest: `still: true` in onion.json emulates prefers-reduced-motion, so the comparison is about the design and not about where the page happened to be scrolled.
A padding that depends on a child being present has no auto-layout equivalent: draw the child in a fixed slot that overhangs the padding, and the padding stays one number.
A variant added by cloning does not inherit its wiring: after adding an axis, check every variant's componentPropertyReferences, or the property silently does nothing on half the set.

An inverse band inside a page is a frame with the tk collection's mode set explicitly to wireframe-inverse and surface/default as its fill; everything inside it, Field instances included, resolves in that context.
A template section is a component whose children are instances of the primitives: Fields, Alert and ArrowCta carry their own properties (Label, Required, Value), so a form is configured, not redrawn.

When Figma and Chromium wrap a paragraph differently by a word, put a soft line break (U+2028) in the text where the browser breaks it; set the width to the real measure, not a width chosen to force the wrap.
A page taller than 1024px cannot be exported whole: export its sections by node id and stitch them at 1x (the skin is still one picture, at native size).

A centred column narrower than the page is its own frame in the design: export the full-width parts and the column separately and compose them at 1x, so the skin stays a single picture at native size.
Three cards at 314.66 fit a 992 row where three at 314.7 wrap (the same 0.1px overhang as HubCards): draw grid cells at the exact fraction.

When a live element is captured to become a design image, hide whatever overlays it in the code (a scrim, a badge) before the screenshot, and draw that overlay in the design as its own layer: otherwise the design carries it twice.
A block that is bottom-anchored in the code (copy over a hero) needs its top set from its height in every variant: auto-layout grows down, the browser grows up.
An absolutely positioned panel is as wide as its anchor unless told otherwise: give it max-content with a floor and a cap, or every label wraps.

A story that decorates the component with padding and flex will stretch a wrapper to the decorator's height: align-items flex-start, or an absolutely positioned panel lands below the stretched box instead of the trigger.
A panel that opens over the page anchors to the element whose edges it follows (the header), not to the cell of it that holds the trigger: anchor it to the cell and it is as wide as the cell.
A state that only exists after a click needs a prop (initialOpen) before it can be photographed: the design cannot be compared with something the story cannot show.
A hairline that sits above every item and below the last is the item's top border plus one closing rule in the list: the last item does not get a different border, the list closes itself.
One instance-swap property can drive two layers: a row's mark and its tag show the same icon, so one Icon property sets both, and the row cannot be configured into disagreeing with itself.

Resizing a vector instance does not scale its stroke weight: for a mark that is drawn at several sizes, build each from the SVG at that size (stroke weights scale with the viewBox) rather than resizing one component.
setBoundVariableForPaint with a variable that was not found does not throw: it binds nothing and the paint goes black. Look the variable up and throw when it is missing, every time.
Capture a live element for the design over the ground the comparison will use (surface-default), or the whole frame differs by the difference between the two grounds.

A Figma gradient is placed by a transform from the frame's normalised space: for a linear one, put the start and end of the CSS gradient line at their normalised positions and invert the matrix; for radial, scale by the farthest-corner radius over the frame's width and height; for angular, rotate by the CSS angle less 90 degrees, because Figma starts at three o'clock and CSS at twelve.
